newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary Postabank draws HUF5.5bln govt guarantee.
newsitem.headline: Hungary Postabank draws HUF5.5bln govt guarantee.

text.p: Hungary's Finance Ministry confirmed on Tuesday press reports that Postabank had asked the government to pay out part of a guarantee on bad loans, worth 5.5 billion forints to the bank.
"The guarantee is due today and last week Postabank informed us that it would be redeemed," Deputy State Secretary Agnes Balazs told a news conference.
Postabank was hit by a wave of deposit withdrawals three months ago which it said had been triggered by rumours.
Later the government undertook to guarantee 12 billion forints in credit and interest owed to the bank by G-Modus Kft, a company founded to collect revenues from Postabank's risky assets.
Balazs said Postabank asked for the redemption of the guarantee as G-Modus had not paid an instalment of the 11 billion forint loan due last week.
The remaining part of the loan is due on July 1, 1998.

The largest shareholders of Postabank contracted with the Finance Ministry to reguarantee the 12 billion forints, and will have to pay 128 million forints' interest on the first 5.5 billion, the whole amount of which must be paid within five years from October 1998, Balazs said.
The two largest shareholders of Postabank, the social security pension and healthcare funds, both have stakes of about 17 percent in Postabank.
The registered capital of Postabank was increased by investors to 23.6 billion forints from 16.5 billion a week ago.
The capital hike increased state influence in the bank, boosting the combined stakes of the two funds, state-owned companies and Szazhalombatta local municipality to above 50 percent.
Postabank and its advisor, SBC Warburg, also invited foreign strategic investors to carry out a second capital rise later this year.
